searchText: reminder: RPC breakout session in 60 mins agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1261 zoom: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82493935220?pwd=wSMSN54Tozw2nB6zrHt5OViZPHmaQM.1 🔥 re: the confusion on infura docs it's actually the correct link, but the branding is for "metamask services" i have shared teh confusion with my corporate overlords Error Codes: use of and interest in error codes is not universal, and today we spec them only when necessary. Improvements to error code specs will be per-rpc-call and not universal across the entire suire of RPCs. Don't assert on error messages! If more precision is needed, specs may combine an error code with sub-codes for situations that require it, via a generic data field in the error response. TODO: collect list of libraries/frameworks/test suits that may be asserting on messages, and involve them in the process to adapt to the coming updated specs that will fix this. Conventions- some situations are not errors, but rather vaguely defined conventions like returning null on an empty search, when an empty list could also be plausible. This likely warrants documentation, but current means of specifying it are sufficient. Data Fields: collecting mis-alignments across clients should be evident via rpc-compat test failures. There are likely a handful of situations where tests have clien-specific assertions to cater to these, and they should be collected and considered for either grandfathering in, or retroactive revision in each client. No strong opinion on the call. Vertical Spike: introducing `eth_fillTransaction` and deprecating `eth_sendTransaction` discussion ongoing and to be continued PSA: keep an eye out for prbot preventing merges, and raise to Pooja Would it also be prudent to advertise these calls to the community in the future? Or perhaps something like the mev-boost community call series can be a thing? I'm mainly asking as there has been a ton of feedback from RPC providers requesting for some place to air grievances or atleast bring up issues they've noticed. We could also just use it as a session at devcon if in person is better for the format. absolutely, we had Infura staff on this one. I think getting more people on the call, especially from the community side, is a very important action point 🙂 We'd need user feedback on the spec also 😄 **RPC Standards Call 0** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uRVG6wkiyqs

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content:
Error Codes: use of and interest in error codes is not universal, and today we spec them only when necessary. Improvements to error code specs will be per-rpc-call and not universal across the entire suire of RPCs.

Don't assert on error messages! If more precision is needed, specs may combine an error code with sub-codes for situations that require it, via a generic data field in the error response.

TODO: collect list of libraries/frameworks/test suits that may be asserting on messages, and involve them in the process to adapt to the coming updated specs that will fix this.

Conventions- some situations are not errors, but rather vaguely defined conventions like returning null on an empty search, when an empty list could also be plausible. This likely warrants documentation, but current means of specifying it are sufficient.

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: Data Fields: collecting mis-alignments across clients should be evident via rpc-compat test failures. There are likely a handful of situations where tests have clien-specific assertions to cater to these, and they should be collected and considered for either grandfathering in, or retroactive revision in each client. No strong opinion on the call.
